messages:
Vikram: quick check — we need to pick a pattern for private tenant routing when we split control plane responsibility. two options: 1) per-tenant private endpoint + regional peering, 2) a lightweight relay in customer VPC (sidecar) with NAT preservation. any strong opinions? :thinking:
Jules: leaning to per-tenant private endpoints. simpler for ops, avoids needing agents in customer subnets. downside = more private endpoints and route table churn, and cost for endpoint ENIs.
Ashley: relay sidecar gives IP preservation (no SNAT) and works for workflows that depend on client IP. but it adds agent lifecycle/rotation complexity.
Ben: if we do endpoints we must solve cross-account route limits. some of our larger customers already hit route table entries when we add per-tenant prefixes. we could do prefix aggregation but that means sacrificing per-tenant isolation.
Vikram: good point. for compliance customers we need strict isolation. can we hybrid? endpoints for high-compliance tenants, sidecars for others?
Jules: hybrid seems practical. open q: how do we decide automatically? based on subscription tier + route count. we should codify in an onboarding policy.
Matt: rollout concerns — sidecars require host networking + iptables SNAT exceptions. sample iptables rule we tested:
```
# preserve source for tenant-relay
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.4.0.0/24 -d 0/0 -j MASQUERADE
# then exempt internal controlplane traffic
iptables -t nat -I POSTROUTING -s 10.4.0.0/24 -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT
```
Ashley: we should avoid host-level hacks if possible. alternative: proxy NAT at the relay process (SO_ORIGINAL_DST) so we don't touch iptables much. less brittle.
infra-bot: Deployment check for branch "feature/tenant-routing-hybrid" completed: 2/3 smoke tests passed, failing test: route-table-limit-sim. See CI link: https://ci.internal/7689
Ben: CI failure confirms concerns. two mitigations: (a) use fewer endpoints with shared advertised prefixes + per-tenant SNI/auth, (b) keep endpoints but offload route count via route aggregation agent. both have tradeoffs.
Vikram: decision proposal: adopt hybrid default. rules:
- Compliance tier -> dedicated private endpoint (one per-tenant)
- Standard tier + small route footprint -> shared endpoint with tenant-specific auth
- Large customers with legacy IP-dependence -> sidecar relay with IP preservation enabled by opt-in
We need a short RFC follow-up to capture this and a rollout plan.
Jules: agree. small additions: add quota guardrails to avoid route-table blowup and a migration tool that can compress/merge endpoints with minimal downtime.
Ashley: add security note: sidecar relays must use mTLS to control plane, and we should encrypt ephemeral tokens in KMS. also audit logs for source IP mapping.
Matt: ops checklist for rollout (first cut):
1) feature flag for hybrid routing
2) onboarding policy automation (tier detection + manual override)
3) migration tool + dry-run mode
4) monitoring: per-tenant route_count gauge, endpoint_enis, relay_cpu
5) canary customers: 3 small, 1 large, 1 compliance tenant
Ben: assign owners? I can take migration tool spike. Jules you can drive onboarding policy. Vikram you oversee canary plan.
Vikram: sounds good — owners: Ben (migration), Jules (onboarding policy + RFC text), Ashley (security requirements), Matt (ops checklist + alerts). I'll draft the RFC follow-up tonight and ping infra for route-sim data.
Jules: note for RFC: include cost delta estimate (ENI per endpoint, NAT gateway usage for relays), and failure modes for controlplane split (eg. endpoint delete vs relay crash).
Ashley: add an example terraform snippet showing shared endpoint + tenant ACL so product can preview: 
```
resource "redwood_private_endpoint" "shared" {
  name = "shared-ep-${var.region}"
  allowed_tenants = ["tenant-a", "tenant-b"]
  auth_policy = "tenant-token"
}
```
Vikram: thanks. action items created in Asana. I'll post RFC link when ready. any blockers?
Ben: none from me. I'll start the spike tomorrow.
Jules: no blockers. +1 to hybrid.
Ashley: no blockers, will draft security checklist.
Matt: I'll wire up the monitoring dashboards once flag is on.
Vikram: OK closing thread for now. RFC will be in #architecture when ready. :thumbsup:
